title: Deterministic time, seeds and reproducible runs

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A nightly route-planning job runs CP-SAT with num_workers = 1, random_seed = 7 and max_time_in_seconds = 60 on a model it never finishes. Two nights with identical input give different plans. What explains it?

options.text: The seed fixes only the first decision, and the later ones vary from run to run
options.says: With one worker and a fixed seed and a work limit, every count repeated, so the decisions themselves repeat.

options.text: The clock limit stopped the same search after different amounts of work
options.says: Right: under a 2-second limit the branches and deterministic time differed between runs.

options.text: The one worker shares plans with helper threads that run at varying speeds
options.says: One worker runs a single search; the one-worker, work-limited runs repeated every number.

options.text: The seed is ignored unless num_workers is left at its default of 0 as well
options.says: The seed works with one worker: seeds 1, 2 and 3 gave three different, repeatable plans.

origin.section: A Wall-Clock Limit Stops the Search at a Different Point Each Run

questions.stem: Runs of a staffing model with num_workers = 8, random_seed = 3 and max_deterministic_time = 5 return a different roster each time. Which change made the eight-worker GridCap runs repeat?

options.text: Replacing the work limit with a time limit of the same number of seconds
options.says: A time limit made even one-worker runs stop at different points.

options.text: Raising the work limit tenfold, so every worker runs to the same end
options.says: A larger limit leaves the race in place; the page made eight workers repeat with interleave_search.

options.text: Setting a different random_seed, since seed 3 is a poor choice for 8 workers
options.says: The 8-worker runs with seed 7 differed too; a seed labels a path but does not stop the race.

options.text: Setting interleave_search, so the workers' tasks run in batches
options.says: Right: with interleave_search, eight workers repeated every number except the wall time.

origin.section: Parallel Workers Race, So Their Plan Can Change Between Runs

questions.stem: Three one-worker solves of a timetabling model, with seeds 1, 2 and 3 and no limit, all end OPTIMAL. What can differ between the three runs?

options.text: The number of branches, while the optimal objective is the same
options.says: Right: on GridCap small the seeds took 3,731, 4,625 and 3,245 branches and all proved $22,741k.

options.text: The optimal objective, since each seed searches a different region
options.says: A proof of optimality does not depend on the path; all three seeds proved the same value.

options.text: Nothing at all, since seeds only matter when there are several workers
options.says: The one-worker runs took different numbers of branches with different seeds.

options.text: Whether a rerun repeats, since a seed makes one-worker runs random
options.says: Each seed's run repeated exactly; a seed labels a path, it does not make the run random.

origin.section: A Seed Changes the Path, Never What Is Proven Optimal

what a different seed changes on a solve that proves optimality
